gen-eater-gf-abeezee: Dark and a little snarling, Eater lays thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems. ABeeZee follows with terminals that stop well clear of the stem, a smooth glassy line that takes the edge off.
gen-eater-gf-aldrich: Aldrich is built like a bent paperclip, its x-height close to the cap height and no thick-thin shifts anywhere. Eater earns its keep big and brief, where its wide gaps and tame contrast can show off.
gen-eater-gf-alexandria: Eater looks dark and aggressive, with short ascenders and wide gaps between letters. Alexandria answers with a tall body, short stems above and below, and wide open c terminals that keep the page easy to move through.
gen-eater-gf-amiko: Moderate shifts in line thickness, with gaps stretched wide between letters, give Eater its menace. Amiko brings low-variation, crayon-tall lowercase and terminals that point outward like tongs, a sturdy modern sans-serif partner.
gen-eater-gf-anek-bangla: Eater brings a dark, aggressive look, with gentle swelling on its curves and short ascenders. And Anek Bangla, a low-contrast sans with wide s curves and a short run from midline to ascender, reads smoothly through paragraph after paragraph.
gen-eater-gf-anek-devanagari: Anek Devanagari has distinctly open letter mouths and a tall middle zone, drawn with very little thickness variation. Eater's stems are only a shade heavier than its arms, so they sit together comfortably.
gen-eater-gf-anek-gujarati: Dark menace meets friendly openness here. Eater leads with thick strokes that guide the eye without dominating it, and Anek Gujarati, a plain sans with lowercase rivaling its capitals and a gaping c, does the quiet reading work.
gen-eater-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Moody and jagged on top, open-handed below. Anek Gurmukhi, a plain sans with big counters in every small letter, takes over from Eater's slightly heavy curves and keeps things clear.
gen-eater-gf-anek-kannada: Anek Kannada reads tall and squared off, like woodblock letters with terminals stopping far from the stem. Eater is best for dark, aggressive emphasis, while the body font handles steady, low-contrast text.
gen-eater-gf-anek-latin: Eater's calm, moderate ratio between stem and thin stroke is oddly restrained for such a dark, aggressive face. Anek Latin does the quieter job, its tall lowercase nearly reaching the capitals and held open.
